paragraphs.source_en: Another analogy with the previous site is the presence, in the next shelter, of an indeterminable down-headed animal (Fig. 5-6). Although it is only a few centimetres in size, it has the same shape as the large animal of Tin Aboteka and it is also associated with masked figures. This enigmatic creature which is discussed in the next section, appears thus in both typologies of sites, namely in the open and hidden site.

paragraphs.source_en: Although this comparison might appear childish, the nomads who still live in the Tassili Plateau, recognise the landscape according to outstanding rock formations by calling them with the most appropriate names according their shapes. The stories connected to mountains and rocks of curious shapes, where they play an active role as if they were human beings, are still very popular among the population of the Sahara. If the contemporary nomads see the landscape as a living thing, a similar behaviour could have existed with the prehistoric populations.
